title: How to Buy Silver for the First Time

segments.narration: New silver buyers often overpay by 20 percent just by choosing the wrong product type.

American Silver Eagles carry 18 to 28 percent above spot. That premium buys USA Mint recognition, not extra silver. A generic round has the same .999 fine silver for 5 to 10 percent over spot. Most first-time buyers pay the Eagle premium without realizing a cheaper option exists.
segments.explanation: American Silver Eagles carry 18-28% above spot for US Mint recognition, not extra silver

segments.narration: Generic 1 oz rounds carry 5 to 10 percent over spot. They have the same .999 fine silver as Eagles. The difference is the name on the coin. A Sunshine Minting round trades near spot on the secondary market and gives you the same silver exposure for less money.
segments.explanation: Generic .999 silver rounds carry only 5-10% over spot, same purity as Eagles

segments.narration: One troy oz weighs 31.1 grams, not 28. Check every delivery on a precision scale. If your 1 oz round weighs 28 grams, you received a fake. A digital scale costs under $10 and confirms every order in 10 seconds.
segments.explanation: One troy oz equals 31.1 grams. Use this to verify weight on every delivery

segments.narration: Most silver dealers add 3 to 4 percent for credit card payments. Paying by check or ACH removes that fee entirely. Most dealer listings show both prices side by side. The check price is the real market rate.
segments.explanation: Most dealers charge 3-4% extra for card payments. Check or ACH eliminates this

segments.narration: Flat-rate shipping costs $9.99 per oz on a single-oz order. Buy 5 oz at once and it drops to $2 per oz. Most dealers offer free shipping over $100 to $199. Buy in batches, not one at a time.
segments.explanation: Shipping drops from $9.99 per oz on single orders to under $2 per oz when buying 5+ oz at once

segments.narration: Standard homeowner policies cap precious metals theft at $1,500. A 10 oz stack at today's prices already costs over $350. By the time you own 50 oz, you have exceeded standard coverage. A scheduled floater costs under $2 per $100 of value per year.
segments.explanation: Standard homeowner policies cap precious metals at $1,500. A modest stack often exceeds this quickly

segments.narration: Pre-1965 USA dimes, quarters, and half dollars are 90 percent silver. Every dollar of face value contains 0.715 troy oz. That fixed ratio makes junk silver easy to price relative to spot. Premiums run 3 to 8 percent, among the lowest available.
segments.explanation: Pre-1965 USA junk silver coins contain 0.715 troy oz of silver per dollar of face value

segments.title: Typical Dealer Premium by Silver Product (Over Spot)
segments.narration: Junk silver and generic rounds sit at 5 to 7 percent over spot. Eagles sit at 18 to 28 percent. On a 5 oz order at $32 spot, the premium difference between rounds and Eagles is about $28. That is silver you did not receive.
